dimensional_exposure.configuration.accep: Accept other players' player dimension-film teleport

Personal client preference, enabled by default and synchronized while connected. Disabling refuses player dimension-film transfers from other players' handheld or stand cameras; your own handheld camera can still teleport you. Ghost projections and photos are unaffected. Stand transfers also obey the stand acceptance setting.

Personal client preference, enabled by default and sent to the server while connected. Allows player dimension-film stands to teleport you when you are in frame. Disabling refuses these transfers while preserving remote viewing, photos and player projections.
dimensional_exposure.configuration.camer: Server settings control the player range for handheld, selfie and stand cameras; client settings control whether stands may teleport you with player dimension film. Player ranges are measured in blocks.
Chunk Unload Delay (§cChange Not Recommended§r)

Server setting. Default: 4; range: 1-120. Measured in subscription generations, each spanning 13 game ticks. Unwatched camera chunks are cleared only after this threshold is exceeded, so this is not an exact duration in seconds. Higher values retain chunks longer and use more memory; low values may cause repeated loading. More than 1200 or 2000 additional chunks caps the delay at 2 or 1 generations respectively. Forced cleanup on respawn or disconnect is unaffected.
Changing this is not recommended: the default balances chunk reuse while switching cameras against memory release.
Check OpenGL Errors

Adds OpenGL error checks during rendering for diagnosing black screens or rendering faults. Log output follows this mod's master logging toggle. Disabled by default. Adds checking overhead; it does not repair rendering errors.
Client Performance Adjustment

Reduces target-dimension distance in vanilla terrain rendering using recent average frame rate and available memory, evaluated every 5 seconds without exceeding the server cap. Disabling removes automatic reduction and does not change video settings or normal world view distance. Sodium uses its own terrain renderer; this setting is not guaranteed to affect it.
Log All Mod Messages

Controls this mod's console and file logs, disabled by default. Enabling records failure diagnostics, warnings and errors while respecting log levels. Disabling also suppresses this mod's warnings and errors without affecting Minecraft or other mods. In-game notices are controlled separately by the runtime warning toggle.
Enable Remote Camera Chunk Loading

Controls whether the server adds loading tickets for additional camera chunks. Enabled by default. Disabling releases existing camera tickets, so views rely on chunks loaded for other reasons and may lack terrain. Re-enabling reloads ranges still being observed. Normal player chunk loading is unaffected.
Show All Runtime Warnings

Enables or disables all in-game runtime warnings, including memory and Iris notices. Enabled by default. Disabling hides these notices without changing memory detection or the master logging toggle; existing chat messages are not removed.
Vanilla View Index Cache Count

Client setting. Retains up to 3 complete view indices per dimension by default; range: 1-16, including the current view. Lower values reduce index cache memory; higher values help reuse indices when returning to recent chunk centers. Render sections and buffers remain independently reused and released after a delay. Changes apply during play. Controls index count, not view distance or server chunk unload delay; has little effect with Sodium.
Reduce Chunk Mesh Buffer Memory

Reduces initial allocation of newly created vanilla chunk mesh buffers, which still grow as needed. Can reduce initial memory for multiple dimensions without changing mesh detail. Existing buffers are not shrunk; restart the client after changing. Sodium's own buffers are not controlled by this setting.
Keep Camera Chunk Tickets Active

Selects the activity level of additional server camera chunk tickets. Enabled by default for entity and block ticking. Disabling only requires block ticking, so creatures may stop updating; subscriptions and loading requests remain. Changes during play release old tickets and reload the camera range at the new level.
Client settings control camera rendering, buffer memory and in-game warnings. Server settings control remote camera chunk loading, ticket activity and unload delay.
dimensional_exposure.configuration.dimen: Server limits for target-dimension views from handheld and manually operated stand cameras, measured in chunks. Client settings control whether other players' player dimension-film cameras may teleport you.
dimensional_exposure.configuration.max_r: Measured as a chunk radius. Default: 8; range: 3-32. Caps remote loading and rendering for handheld and manual stand cameras, also limited by client requests and server view distance. Radius 3 subscribes to at most 7x7 chunks; radius 8 to at most 17x17. Performance adjustment may further reduce rendering distance. Creature search range is measured separately in blocks and is not cropped by this setting.
dimensional_exposure.configuration.mob_c: Measured in blocks. Default: 16; range: 1-32. Expands the target camera block's search box by this amount along X, Y and Z, then selects unobstructed creatures within the lens view. Shared by handheld, manual stand and redstone stand captures. Independent of view distance; lower values reduce entity search work.
dimensional_exposure.configuration.mob_d: Controls the target-dimension entity search range for creature dimension film. Entities must also pass the lens frustum, focal-length and obstruction checks.
dimensional_exposure.configuration.stand: Server setting in blocks. Default: 8; range: 1-64. Controls source-world ghost projections, player dimension-film candidates and source-player chunk subscriptions for handheld, selfie and manually operated stand cameras. Transfer candidates must also pass lens frustum and obstruction checks. Changes automatically update active viewfinders. Redstone photos still show the normal source world: this setting only limits player selection and does not crop those photos. Target-dimension view distance is configured separately.
